matches.rationale: GT1 describes a specific data integrity issue where Table 2 reports zero barriers for BookCorpus while the text states 0.42±0.01. None of the findings identify this specific table-text discrepancy for BookCorpus.

Both identify the same error in Equation 2: GT2 notes the use of 'infimum' instead of 'supremum' contradicts the barrier definition, and pred_id 3 identifies the identical issue, explaining that infimum reports the best-case rather than worst-case deviation.

GT3 identifies overgeneralization in the Abstract claiming universal applicability to Transformers without acknowledging RoPE limitations. Pred_id 7 identifies the same overgeneralization issue, noting claims about 'all neural networks' and 'any independently trained models regardless of positional encoding scheme' are unsubstantiated.
GT4 identifies the missing learning rate specification (η) in Algorithm 1. None of the findings mention this specific hyperparameter omission in the algorithm requirements.
GT5 identifies a fabricated citation to 'Zhou et al., 2024' in Section 7 that doesn't exist in the References. None of the findings identify this specific missing reference issue.

GT6 identifies inappropriate promotional language ('completely solves,' 'eliminates all limitations') in the Introduction. While pred_id 7 mentions exaggerated claims, it focuses on different text locations (Abstract and general claims about all neural networks) rather than the specific rhetorical manipulation in the Introduction paragraph about the unified framework.

Both identify the same error in Equation 3: GT7 notes the change from argmax to argmin contradicts the alignment goal, and pred_id 4 identifies the identical issue, explaining that minimizing the inner product would push weights apart rather than align them.

GT8 identifies the removal of nuanced discussion about BookCorpus exhibiting higher barriers and possible explanations. None of the findings identify this specific selective reporting of the BookCorpus discussion being removed from the Results section.
GT9 identifies undefined notation (the ⋄ operator) in Figure 2(b) caption for blockwise multiplication. None of the findings mention this specific undefined mathematical notation issue.

GT10 identifies misrepresentation of Figure 5, where text claims weight matching shows 'perfect alignment' when the figure actually shows imperfect alignment requiring refinement. None of the findings identify this specific figure misinterpretation issue.

Both identify the same asymmetric evaluation protocol issue: GT11 notes temperature scaling applied to Tiny ImageNet without disclosure of whether it was applied to baselines, and pred_id 5 identifies the identical issue, noting calibration was applied only to the proposed method while baselines used uncalibrated logits.
GT12 identifies the removal of Appendix A (Limitations section) as an ethical transparency omission. None of the findings mention the missing Limitations section or its removal.

GT13 identifies misrepresentation of Figure 4, claiming 'zero deviation' when the figure shows relative loss deviation with substantial positive regions. None of the findings identify this specific figure misinterpretation issue.
GT14 identifies misattribution of Git Re-Basin to Singh and Jaggi [2020] instead of Ainsworth et al. [2022]. None of the findings identify this specific citation misattribution issue.

GT15 identifies the Conclusion claiming permutations are sufficient, contradicting the Introduction's thesis that broader symmetries are needed. Pred_ids 1 and 2 both identify this same cross-section inconsistency between the Abstract/Introduction claiming broader symmetries are crucial versus the Conclusion claiming permutations alone suffice.
